title: Beyond Twenty Questions: Semantic Limits and Query Complexity of Universal Concept Identification
domain: information theory / active learning / lexical semantics / ontology / philosophy of language / computational cognition
summary: A formal and empirical research program asking what semantic structure is necessary to identify arbitrary human-representable concepts under finite query budgets, how much natural semantic questions cost relative to unrestricted information-theoretic queries, and where identification fails for vague, contextual, empty, contradictory, self-referential, undecidable, or ineffable targets.

aris.provenance: ARIS4C guided design, live prior-art audit, and combinatorial Pilot 0; full empirical-run provenance to be frozen at Benchmark v0
